title: Mutable Value Objects
pattern: A class/struct representing a descriptive aspect of the domain (no conceptual identity) designed with public mutable setters or in-place modifiers.
why_bad: If value objects are mutable, sharing them across entities can lead to side-effects where updating one reference silently corrupts another entity's state, violating model invariants [385:385].
detection: Types classified as Value Objects (e.g., Money, Dimensions, Addresses) that expose public mutable fields or methods that mutate self-state instead of returning a new instance [385:385].
fix: Design Value Objects as completely immutable. Modify state solely by replacing the entire instance [385:385].
source: *Refactoring* (Fowler), Chapter 3: Value Objects [385:385]; *Domain-Driven Design* (Evans), Value Objects [9:350].
